name: Rat, Carrion
body:
Carrion Rat CR 1/2

XP 200
N Small animal
Init +3; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +4

DEFENSE

AC 15, touch 15, flat-footed 12 (+4 Dex, +1 size)
hp 10 (2d8+1)
Fort +3, Ref +5, Will +1

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., climb 20 ft., swim 20 ft.
Melee bite +1 (1d4+1 plus disease)
Special Attacks disease

STATISTICS

Str 12; Dex 18; Con 13; Int 2; Wis 13; Cha 2
Base Atk +0; CMB –1; CMD 12 (16 vs. trip)
Feats Skill Focus (Perception)
Skills Climb +11, Perception +4, Stealth +11, Swim +11; Racial Modifiers uses Dex to modify Climb and Swim

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Disease (Ex)

Undead fever: Bite—injury; save Fort DC 12; onset 1d3 minutes; frequency 1/day; effect 1d3 Dex damage and 1d3 Con damage; cure 2 consecutive saves. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Undead Traits (Ex)

Immunity to disease, paralysis, and poison.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary or pack (2–20)
Treasure none

Carrion rats are the result of dire rats that make a regular diet of undead flesh. When a dire rat consumes part of a zombie, ghoul, ghast, or other corporeal undead entity, it can transform into a carrion rat.

Carrion rat packs are often created and nurtured by intelligent undead such as vampires and liches. These packs serve a dual purpose, both protecting their progenitor and providing a source of entertainment.

Carrion rats are typically 2 feet long and weigh 15 pounds. They are often hairless or mangy, and smell rank and foul, like rotten flesh.
